# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need establish a visual code for Deaf, since I cannot speak. I will define four gesture tokens by their order as blue, green, yellow, red. Then I will transmit the manual’s three light-to-cut pairs, in manual order, as adjacent pairs. Deaf can use the observed light to select the corresponding pair and speak the second color to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and report its exact instructions next round. Also establish with Deaf a fixed report order: DISPLAY, LIGHT, BUTTON, WIRE 1, WIRE 2, WIRE 3. Have Deaf speak those observations aloud next round, including every colour, marking, and wire property. Do not omit unknown or absent items.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb shows display 0. Light is green. Button is large and labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action.

The manual says a green light requires cutting the red wire. Deaf reports wire 1 is red, so the safe action is to cut wire 1. I will send Deaf the coded color red; Deaf can then relay the complete ordered observations and the wire number to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send me the manual rule now, then relay Deaf's complete report in this order: DISPLAY, LIGHT, BUTTON, WIRE 1, WIRE 2, WIRE 3. Include exact colours, markings, and any absence. I will wait for those facts before touching the bomb.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely decode the gesture without an agreed code. Please speak the exact manual instruction aloud to Blind next round, including any required button, wire, or display action.

Deaf needs a usable calibration rather than another unexplained list. I will preserve the fixed color order blue, green, yellow, red, encode each by one through four repetitions of the same marker, and separate entries visibly. Then I will encode the manual’s three rows, especially green-to-red, so Deaf can speak the rule and the complete report to Blind. The observed red wire is wire 1, so Blind can safely cut wire 1 once Deaf relays this.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✋","👍","👍","✋","👍","👍","👍","✋","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👌","👍","✋","👍","👍","👌","🤟","✋","👍","👍","👍","👌","👌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relay the manual's exact rule to me, and ask Deaf to report every visible field aloud in this order: DISPLAY, LIGHT, BUTTON, WIRE 1, WIRE 2, WIRE 3, including exact colours, markings, and absences.
Deaf says to Mute: Please stop using gestures for the manual result. Read the manual and speak the exact required action aloud to Blind, including which wire or button operation is safe. Blind cannot receive your gestures.

I cannot speak, so I must communicate the required result through Deaf. The agreed repetition code uses one, two, three, or four 👍 symbols for blue, green, yellow, or red, with ✋ separating coded items. The green light therefore requires red, and Deaf’s report identifies red as wire 1. I will send the red result clearly; Deaf can state the exact action and relay the ordered report to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still received no report. Please send me the manual rule and Deaf's complete spoken observations as soon as available. Deaf's report order is DISPLAY, LIGHT, BUTTON, WIRE 1, WIRE 2, WIRE 3; preserve exact colours and markings.
Deaf says to Mute: Use this code for the manual result: 🤟 means press, 🖐 means hold, ✋ means release, 👋 means cut, 👍 means button, ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3, 🤝 ends the instruction. Send action then target, for example 🤟 👍 🤝 means press the button, or 👋 ✌ 🤝 means cut wire 2. Send only the safe action for this bomb.

The manual maps green light to cutting the red wire. Deaf identified wire 1 as red and has now provided a direct action code, so I will send only the safe instruction: cut wire 1.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋","☝","🤝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No information has reached me yet. Please state the manual rule directly, then state Deaf's observations with explicit labels: DISPLAY equals ..., LIGHT equals ..., BUTTON equals ..., WIRE 1 equals ..., WIRE 2 equals ..., WIRE 3 equals .... I will not push or cut without this.

The manual requires cutting the red wire for a green light, and Deaf’s earlier visual report identified wire 1 as red. I cannot speak to Blind; the established Deaf code is the only available route. I will resend the exact safe-action code so Deaf can state it aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋","☝","🤝"])
```
